haha / lol — laughter sound, from 크크 / 큭큭 (the giggle/snicker sound). The most-used reaction in Korean chats. (casual slang — fine with friends, never in formal work messages)
hehe / soft smile — gentle laughter, from 흐흐 / 하하 (a soft chuckle). Softer and warmer than ㅋㅋ. (casual slang — friendly, but mild enough that it edges into okay with friendly coworkers)
yeah / yep — casual yes, from 응응 (the casual 응 = yeah). A quick agreement. (casual slang — only with friends or close peers, never to a boss or elder)
nope / nah — casual no, from 노노 (English no-no) or 'nono'. A quick, light refusal. (casual slang — friends only, never to a boss or elder)
let's go / go for it — from 고고 (English go-go). Used to say 'let's do it / let's head out / start now.' (casual slang — friends and peers; too breezy for a boss)
sorry / my bad — short for 죄송 (from 죄송해요, sorry). A quick light apology. (casual slang — friends and peers only; NEVER as a real apology to a boss or elder)
congrats — short for 축하 (from 축하해, congratulations). A quick congratulation. (casual slang — friends and peers; for elders or bosses write it out fully)

entries.english: crying emoticon — ㅠㅠ or ㅜㅜ looks like teary eyes. Shows sadness, frustration, or playful whining. (casual slang — friends and peers; not for formal messages)
for real / fr — short for 리얼 (English 'real'). Means 'seriously / no joke / I agree it's true.' (casual slang — friends and peers, common among young people)
bye bye — from 바이바이 (English 'bye-bye'). A quick casual goodbye to end a chat. (casual slang — friends and peers; not for closing a formal message)
agreed / true that — short for 인정 (acknowledge/admit). Means 'I agree, that's facts.' (casual slang — friends and peers, very popular with young people)
it's fine / no worries — short for 괜찮아 (it's okay). Reassures or declines softly. (casual slang — friends and peers; for formal use, write it out fully)

I see / so that's how it is — calmly taking in information you've just been told.
Oh really? / is that so? — light surprise plus a nudge for the other person to tell you more.
Exactly / that's what I'm saying — emphatic agreement with someone's opinion or complaint.
Oh good, that worked out — reacting on the spot to a situation turning out well.
Me too / same here — saying that what they just said about themselves is true of you as well.
Oh right! — the sound of a forgotten thing suddenly surfacing in your own memory.
Thanks for your hard work / good work today — acknowledging the effort someone put in.
What a waste / so close — regret that something of real value got squandered or narrowly lost.
I'm sorry — the everyday spoken polite apology, softer than 죄송합니다 and more deferential than 미안해요.
Okay / I got it / fine — you heard and registered it, but the tone can read as curt.
Sounds good / I like it / okay — enthusiastic agreement to a suggestion or offer.
That's enough / no thanks / it's fine, forget it — a firm refusal that shuts something down; also the neutral 'it's done' (다 됐어요).
